One concrete false green needs fixing: the removal-edge tolerance accepts missing NoteOffs that the scheduler ordering cannot justify. Otherwise, the assertions fit the scoped stopped-panic contract.

- **Evidence:** [panic_hotplug_trace.py:24](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/tests/behaviour/panic_hotplug_trace.py:24) uses `abs(len(prefix)-len(reference))<=16`. I loaded the supplied M-PANIC-014 native sweep and removed its final 16 port-1 messages before disconnection. The verifier still passed with prefix **416**, while port 2 had emitted **432**. Removing just one also passed. An application omission would retain contiguous native sequence numbers, so that separate check would not catch it.
- **Why this exceeds legitimate interleaving:** [m_midi.lua:434](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/m_midi.lua:434) schedules ports in ascending order; [scheduler.lua:46](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/scheduler.lua:46) resumes jobs in creation order; [m_midi.lua:425](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/lib/m_midi.lua:425) yields after each 16-message pitch. Before removal, port 1 can lead port 2 by up to 16 messages, but cannot trail it.
- **Minimal fix:** require `0 <= len(prefix)-len(reference) <= 16`. Add rejection tests deleting 1 and 16 messages from the connected prefix tail. The existing [edge test:32](/home/andy/projects/mosaic-behaviour-tests/tests/behaviour/test_panic_hotplug_trace.py:32) deletes 20 messages, missing this hole. No application semantics change is needed.

All six existing unit tests passed. The four supplied manifests report controlled-experimental passes; I make no claim about the active real-time runner.

**CONFIDENCE: High.** Different coroutine ordering could change the proposed bound; the current code explicitly fixes that ordering.
